questions.title: South Africa's National Budget — Revenue, Expenditure and Reading a Graph

subQuestions.questionText: State the difference between a budget and an income and expenditure statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
A budget is used to plan future (expected) income and expenditure, while an income and expenditure statement records the actual amounts of income and expenditure for the period.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: As a percentage of GDP, the budget shows Tax revenue at 24,8% and Main budget revenue at 24,7%. Identify which of the consolidated budget's revenue sources is lower.
subQuestions.memoText:
Main budget revenue (24,7%)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name two sources of tax revenue listed in this budget.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any two of: Personal income tax; Corporate income tax; Value-added tax; Taxes on international trade and transactions.

[Award 2 marks — 1 per correct source]

subQuestions.questionText: The tax revenue sources are: Personal income tax R687,9 bn; Corporate income tax R308,3 bn; Value-added tax R539,7 bn; Taxes on international trade and transactions R62,5 bn. Show, using calculations, how the total of R1 598,4 bn for tax revenue was calculated.
subQuestions.memoText:
R687,9 + R308,3 + R539,7 + R62,5 = R1 598,4 billion

Mark 1: adding all four tax revenue values
Mark 2: all values listed correctly to give R1 598,4 bn

subQuestions.questionText: An amount −R43,7 (SACU payments) appears with a minus sign in the amount column. State the importance of the minus sign.
subQuestions.memoText:
The minus sign shows that R43,7 billion is not income — it is a payment (a deduction/subtraction) that is taken away from the revenue.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The main budget revenue sources total R1 588,0 billion. Write out this value in full, without using commas or words.
subQuestions.memoText:
R1 588 000 000 000

Mark 1: identifying R1 588 billion
Mark 2: correct place value (R1 588 000 000 000)

subQuestions.questionText: Write down, in words, the amount in full for non-tax revenue (R33,3 billion).
subQuestions.memoText:
Thirty-three billion, three hundred million rand.

Mark 1: thirty-three billion
Mark 2: three hundred million rand

subQuestions.label: 1.1.8 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Convert the given tax revenue percentage of GDP (24,8%) to a decimal number.
subQuestions.memoText:
24,8 ÷ 100 = 0,248

Mark 1: dividing by 100
Mark 2: 0,248 (no percentage symbol)

subQuestions.label: 1.1.8 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the acronym for Value-added tax.
subQuestions.memoText:
VAT

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: A bar graph shows Learning and Culture Expenditure for 2022/2023 (total R430,9 bn): Basic Education R282,80 bn; University Transfers R48,70 bn; National Student Financial Aid Scheme R46,10 bn; Skills development levy institutions R21,70 bn; Technical & vocational education and training R12,60 bn; Education administration (amount not shown). List the sector that spent the least amount of the total learning and culture budget.
subQuestions.memoText:
Technical & vocational education and training (R12,60 billion)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine how much was spent on the skills development levy institutions sector.
subQuestions.memoText:
R21,70 billion (R21 700 000 000)

[Award 2 marks for reading the value from the graph]

subQuestions.questionText: Name another graph that can be used to represent the above data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any one of: pie chart; vertical bar graph; dot plot; line graph; pictograph.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of the total Learning and Culture Expenditure (R430,9 bn) that is spent on Basic Education (R282,80 bn).
State which sector spent the second-largest amount of the Learning and Culture Expenditure budget.
subQuestions.memoText:
University Transfers (R48,70 billion) — Basic Education is the largest, University Transfers is the second largest.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the missing amount for the Education administration sector, given the total is R430,9 bn.
subQuestions.memoText:
= R430,9 − R282,80 − R48,70 − R46,10 − R21,70 − R12,60
= R19 billion (R19 000 000 000)

Mark 1: subtracting the known sector values from R430,9 bn
Mark 2: answer R19 billion

subQuestions.questionText: Arrange the given data values (the six sector amounts) in descending order of value.
subQuestions.memoText:
R282,80 billion; R48,70 billion; R46,10 billion; R21,70 billion; R19 billion; R12,60 billion.

Mark 1: values in order
Mark 2: descending order correct, using 'billion'

questions.title: Nike Shoes and a Shoe-Size Data Set — Discount, VAT, Exchange Rates and Scatter Plots

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Nike was founded in January 1964. Calculate the total number of years Nike has been in business as at 2023. Round your answer to the nearest year.
subQuestions.memoText:
2023 − 1964 = 59, + 1 (founded in January, so a full year has passed) = 60 years
(Accept 59 years — 1 mark only.)

Mark 1: 2023 − 1964
Mark 2: 60 years

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: The Christmas special ran from 23 December 2022 to 6 January 2023. Determine the total number of days this Christmas special was on for.
subQuestions.memoText:
December: 23–31 = 9 days; January: 1–6 = 6 days
Total = 9 + 6 = 15 days
(Accept 14 days — 1 mark only.)

Mark 1: 9 days in December
Mark 2: 15 days total

subQuestions.questionText: The 'Nike Air Jordan 1 Retro High Tie Dye' shoes normally cost R2 299 and were advertised at R1 499 during the special. Calculate the amount of discount offered on these shoes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Discount = R2 299 − R1 499 = R800

Mark 1: subtraction
Mark 2: answer R800

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage discount you would receive if you were to purchase these shoes during the advertised special (normal price R2 299, discount R800).
subQuestions.memoText:
% discount = R800 ÷ R2 299 × 100 = 34,80%

Mark 1: R800 as the numerator
Mark 2: ÷ R2 299
Mark 3: × 100 → 34,80%

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the amount of VAT on the discounted price of R1 499 (including 15% VAT).
subQuestions.memoText:
Price excluding VAT = R1 499 ÷ 1,15 = R1 303,48
VAT = R1 499 − R1 303,48 = R195,52
(OR R1 499 × 15/115 = R195,52)

Mark 1: dividing R1 499 by 1,15
Mark 2: subtracting the VAT-exclusive amount
Mark 3: answer R195,52

subQuestions.label: 2.1.5 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the exchange rate $1 : R17,006289 to convert R1 499 into US dollars. Round off your answer to two decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
= R1 499 ÷ 17,006289
= $88,14386
= $88,14

Mark 1: dividing R1 499 by 17,006289
Mark 2: $88,14386
Mark 3: rounding to two decimal places → $88,14

subQuestions.label: 2.1.5 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain why currency exchange rates are often written with many decimal digits.
subQuestions.memoText:
When large amounts of foreign currency are converted, the number of decimal places in the exchange rate noticeably affects the final answer, so more decimal places give a more accurate conversion.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: A learner collected shoe sizes and heights (cm) from female students: (6; 152), (7; 169), (8; 174), (4; 170), (8; 177), (5; 158), (10; 183), (8; 170), (12; 188), (6; 162), (9; 180). Determine the median shoe size for this data set.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ordered shoe sizes: 4; 5; 6; 6; 7; 8; 8; 8; 9; 10; 12
11 values → the 6th value is the median = 8

Mark 1: ordering the data
Mark 2: median = 8

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the modal shoe size for this data set.
subQuestions.memoText:
8 (it appears three times, more often than any other size).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the range for the heights in this data set (heights range from 152 cm to 188 cm).
subQuestions.memoText:
Range = 188 cm − 152 cm = 36 cm

Mark 1: max − min
Mark 2: answer 36 cm

subQuestions.questionText: Use the given data to draw a scatter graph (scatter plot) of height (cm) against shoe size on the grid provided. State the key features your graph must show.
subQuestions.memoText:
A heading, e.g. "Student Shoe Size vs Height".
Eleven points plotted from the data pairs: (6; 152), (7; 169), (8; 174), (4; 170), (8; 177), (5; 158), (10; 183), (8; 170), (12; 188), (6; 162), (9; 180).
Axes: shoe size on the horizontal axis, height in cm on the vertical axis.

Mark 1: heading
Mark 2: correct scatter-plot form (points, not joined)
Marks 3–8: plotting the points in pairs correctly, including the outlier point(s)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe an observable trend in your scatter graph.
subQuestions.memoText:
There is a positive trend (positive correlation): as shoe size increases, height tends to increase.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 2.2.6 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Define an outlier in a data set.
subQuestions.memoText:
An outlier is a data point that differs significantly (much bigger or much smaller) from the other observations in the data set.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 2.2.6 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify a possible outlier in this data set. Give the shoe size and corresponding height.
subQuestions.memoText:
Shoe size 4; height 170 cm (a small shoe size with an unusually tall height).
OR shoe size 6; height 152 cm (short for that shoe size).

Mark 1: correct shoe size
Mark 2: correct corresponding height

questions.title: Loadshedding — Stacked Bar Graphs, Percentage Increase and Hire Purchase

subQuestions.questionText: A stacked bar graph shows the hours of national loadshedding per year by stage. The 2015 bar totals about 800 hours, of which the Stage 1 portion is 400 hours. Determine how many hours of Stage 2 loadshedding occurred in 2015.
subQuestions.memoText:
Stage 2 hours = 800 − 400 = 400 hours

Mark 1: subtracting the Stage 1 portion from the 2015 total
Mark 2: answer 400 hours

subQuestions.questionText: The 2021 bar shows 1 153 hours of loadshedding, labelled as '48 days'. Show, using calculations, how the 48 days was calculated for 2021.
subQuestions.memoText:
= 1 153 ÷ 24
= 48,04
≈ 48 days

Mark 1: dividing 1 153 by 24
Mark 2: 48,04 ≈ 48 days

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage increase in the number of hours of loadshedding from 2018 (124 hours) to 2022 (1 637 hours). Use: Percentage increase = ((New value − Old value) ÷ Old value) × 100%.
Give ONE possible reason why there are no bars drawn for the years 2016 and 2017.
subQuestions.memoText:
There was no loadshedding during 2016 and 2017. (Also accept: no data was recorded for those years; or there was some loadshedding but too little to plot at the given scale.)

[Award 2 marks for one valid reason]

subQuestions.questionText: Francois Nel buys a home loadshedding kit. The cash price is R44 956,52 excluding VAT. Using calculations, show that the cash price, including 15% VAT, is R51 700.

The hire purchase agreement requires a deposit of 10% of the cash price (including VAT, R51 700). Calculate the loan amount, including VAT, for the hire purchase agreement. Loan Amount = Cash Price − Deposit Value.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The hire purchase agreement is over 3 years at an interest rate of 8% p.a. (simple interest) on the loan amount of R46 530. Calculate the total cost of the loan if the loadshedding kit was purchased on hire purchase.
subQuestions.memoText:
Interest = R46 530 × 8% × 3 = R3 722,40 × 3 = R11 167,20
Total cost of the loan = R46 530 + R11 167,20 = R57 697,20

Mark 1: simple interest at 8%
Mark 2: × 3 years
Mark 3: R11 167,20 interest
Mark 4: adding to the loan amount → R57 697,20

subQuestions.label: 3.2.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the monthly instalment that Francois Nel would pay if this kit was purchased on hire purchase (total cost of the loan R57 697,20, over 3 years).
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of months = 3 × 12 = 36
Monthly instalment = R57 697,20 ÷ 36 = R1 602,70

Mark 1: 36 months
Mark 2: dividing R57 697,20 by 36
Mark 3: answer R1 602,70

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the amount Francois Nel would have saved if he purchased the kit for cash (R46 530 loan value equivalent) instead of the hire purchase agreement (total cost R57 697,20).
subQuestions.memoText:
Saving = R57 697,20 − R46 530 = R11 167,20
(OR R57 697,20 + R5 170 deposit − R51 700 cash price = R11 167,20)

Mark 1: subtraction
Mark 2: answer R11 167,20

subQuestions.questionText: Give another legal way that Francois Nel could finance this loadshedding kit instead of the hire purchase agreement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any one of: take a personal loan from the bank; borrow against (add to) his home loan; borrow money from a family member; use a credit card; use lay-by.

[Award 2 marks for one valid method]

questions.title: Prime Interest Rate and Home Loans — Inflation, Mean, Probability and Cost of Credit

subQuestions.questionText: Define inflation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Inflation is the ongoing (monthly / yearly) increase in the prices of goods and services. It can also be described as a decrease in the purchasing power of money over time.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The graph shows 11 prime interest rate values over the period, which add up to 92,75. Calculate the mean prime interest rate over the period shown.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mean = 92,75 ÷ 11 = 8,43%

Mark 1: sum of all the values (92,75)
Mark 2: ÷ 11
Mark 3: answer 8,43%

subQuestions.label: 4.1.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Describe the impact on an individual who took a loan of R100 000 from a bank linked to the prime interest rate in 2019. Support your answer with calculations using the interest rates provided on the graph (prime rose from about 7,75% to about 10,75%).
subQuestions.memoText:
At the lower rate: R100 000 × 7,75% = R7 750 interest per year
At the higher rate: R100 000 × 10,75% = R10 750 interest per year
As the prime rate increased, the interest charged and the monthly repayments on the loan increased (by about R3 000 per year on R100 000), so the loan became more expensive for the individual.

Mark 1: R100 000 × 7,75%
Mark 2: R100 000 × 10,75%
Mark 3: comparing the two amounts
Mark 4: conclusion — repayments / interest increase

subQuestions.questionText: Does increasing the prime interest rate have the desired effect of decreasing the inflation rate? Use values and dates from the graph to support your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Yes, it does. The interest rate was increased from July 2022, and after that the inflation rate slowly started to decrease, from 7,8% down to 6,9%.

Mark 1: yes
Mark 2: interest rate increased in July 2022
Mark 3: inflation rate fell from 7,8% to 6,9%

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability of randomly choosing a prime interest rate of 9% from the 11 prime interest rates given (one of which is 9%). Give your answer as a percentage rounded off to two decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
P(9%) = 1 ÷ 11 × 100 = 9,09%

Mark 1: 1 (the number of 9% values)
Mark 2: ÷ 11 (total values)
Mark 3: × 100
Mark 4: rounded to 2 decimal places → 9,09%

subQuestions.questionText: Bheki Zulu pays a 15% deposit and takes out a home loan of R1 000 000 to cover the balance. Calculate the total cash price of Bheki Zulu's house.
subQuestions.memoText:
The loan covers 85% of the price (100% − 15% deposit).
Price = R1 000 000 ÷ 85% = R1 000 000 ÷ 0,85 = R1 176 470,59

Mark 1: recognising the loan is 85% of the price
Mark 2: dividing R1 000 000 by 0,85
Mark 3: answer R1 176 470,59

subQuestions.label: 4.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: For the R1 000 000 loan over 20 years, the required monthly instalment is R8 364,40 and the number of months to repay is 240. Calculate the total cost of credit if he takes his home loan over 20 years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total cost of credit = R8 364,40 × 240 = R2 007 456

Mark 1: reading the R8 364,40 monthly instalment
Mark 2: multiplying by 240
Mark 3: answer R2 007 456

subQuestions.label: 4.2.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total interest he pays on his home loan over 20 years (total cost of credit R2 007 456 on a R1 000 000 loan).
subQuestions.memoText:
Total interest = R2 007 456 − R1 000 000 = R1 007 456

Mark 1: subtracting R1 000 000
Mark 2: answer R1 007 456

subQuestions.label: 4.2.2 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: For the R1 000 000 loan over 30 years, the total cost of credit is R2 641 554. How much more would Bheki Zulu pay if he pays his home loan over 30 years instead of 20 years?
subQuestions.memoText:
Total interest over 30 years = R2 641 554 − R1 000 000 = R1 641 554
Extra paid = R1 641 554 − R1 007 456 = R634 098
(OR R2 641 554 − R2 007 456 = R634 098)

Mark 1: interest over 30 years = R1 641 554
Mark 2: subtracting the 20-year interest
Mark 3: answer R634 098

subQuestions.questionText: Give another reason, besides the interest payable, that Bheki Zulu would need to consider when deciding to take his home loan over 20 or 30 years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Monthly affordability — can he afford the higher monthly repayment of the 20-year bond? (Also accept: his age or health over the length of the bond term.)

[Award 2 marks for one valid reason]

questions.title: Billy Joel's Salary Slip — Correcting a Tax Calculation and a Box-and-Whisker Plot

subQuestions.questionText: Billy Joel earns a gross salary of R21 500 per month. His friend Tom calculated Billy's annual tax as: Tax = R42 678 + 26%(237 100); Tax = R142 260 + R17 235; Tax = R159 495. Tom made two errors. Identify these two errors and explain how each can be rectified.
subQuestions.memoText:
Error (i): Tom used 26% of R237 100. He should use 26% of (annual taxable income − R237 100), i.e. he must first subtract R237 100 from Billy's annual salary and take 26% of the difference.
Error (ii): Tom added the primary rebate (R17 235). The rebate must be subtracted, not added.
(A third slip: 26% × R237 100 ≠ R142 260 — the multiplication is also wrong.)

Mark 1: identifying error (i)
Mark 2: how to rectify (i) — subtract R237 100 from the annual salary first
Mark 3: identifying error (ii) — the rebate was added
Mark 4: how to rectify (ii) — subtract the rebate

subQuestions.label: 5.1.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the SARS tax table to calculate Billy Joel's annual tax for 2023/2024. He earns R21 500 per month. Bracket R237 101 – R370 500: R42 678 + 26% of taxable income above R237 100. Primary rebate: R17 235. Show all working.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual salary = R21 500 × 12 = R258 000
Bracket: R237 101 – R370 500
Tax = R42 678 + 26% × (R258 000 − R237 100)
= R42 678 + 0,26 × R20 900
= R42 678 + R5 434
= R48 112
Less primary rebate: R48 112 − R17 235 = R30 877 per year

Mark 1: R21 500 × 12 = R258 000
Mark 2: correct tax bracket
Mark 3: R258 000 − R237 100
Mark 4: 26% of the excess
Mark 5: + R42 678
Mark 6: subtracting the rebate → R30 877

subQuestions.label: 5.1.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Has Billy Joel been paying the correct monthly tax? His salary slip shows PAYE of R2 573,08 per month. Use calculations to support your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Monthly tax = R30 877 ÷ 12 = R2 573,08
This equals the R2 573,08 shown on his salary slip.
Yes, Billy Joel has been paying the correct amount of tax.

Mark 1: R30 877 ÷ 12
Mark 2: R2 573,08
Mark 3: conclusion — yes, it is correct

subQuestions.questionText: A box-and-whisker diagram shows the costs of servicing 50 different cars at the workshop. Write down the median cost of servicing these cars.
subQuestions.memoText:
R6 000

[Award 2 marks for the correct value (with the rand unit) read from the diagram]

subQuestions.label: 5.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: On the box-and-whisker diagram, R3 700 is the lower quartile. Determine the probability of randomly selecting a car costing more than R3 700 to service. Write your answer as a simplified fraction.
subQuestions.memoText:
R3 700 is the lower quartile, so 75% of the cars cost more than R3 700.
P(> R3 700) = 75/100 = 3/4

Mark 1: numerator 75
Mark 2: denominator 100
Mark 3: simplifying to 3/4

subQuestions.label: 5.2.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the number of cars (out of the 50) that cost more than R3 700 to service.
subQuestions.memoText:
= 50 × 75%
= 37,5
≈ 38 cars

Mark 1: 50 × 75%
Mark 2: 37,5
Mark 3: 38 whole cars

subQuestions.questionText: The lower quartile is R3 700 and the upper quartile is R7 950. Calculate the interquartile range.
subQuestions.memoText:
IQR = R7 950 − R3 700 = R4 250

Mark 1: Q3 = R7 950
Mark 2: Q3 − Q1
Mark 3: answer R4 250

subQuestions.questionText: Billy made the following statement: "Less than 25% of cars cost more than R12 500 to service." This statement is incorrect. Use the data given (upper quartile = R7 950) to correct this statement: "Less than 25% of cars cost more than ______ to service."
subQuestions.memoText:
"Less than 25% of cars cost more than R7 950 to service."
(R7 950 is the upper quartile — only the top 25% of the data lies above it.)

Mark 1: identifying the upper quartile
Mark 2: R7 950
